{{Short description|Study of systems of inequalitites}}
In [[mathematics]], '''real algebraic geometry''' is the sub-branch of [[algebraic geometry]] studying real [[algebraic set]]s, i.e. [[real number|real-number]] solutions to [[algebraic equation]]s with real-number coefficients, and [[map (mathematics)|mappings]] between them (in particular [[real polynomial mapping]]s).

'''Semialgebraic geometry''' is the study of [[semialgebraic set]]s, i.e. real-number solutions to algebraic [[inequality (mathematics)|inequalities]] with-real number coefficients, and mappings between them. The most natural mappings between semialgebraic sets are [[semialgebraic mapping]]s, i.e., mappings whose graphs are semialgebraic sets.

==Terminology==

Nowadays the words 'semialgebraic geometry' and 'real algebraic geometry' are used as synonyms, because real algebraic sets cannot be studied seriously without the use of semialgebraic sets. For example, a projection of a real algebraic set along a coordinate axis need not be a real algebraic set, but it is always a semialgebraic set: this is the [[Tarski–Seidenberg theorem]].<ref>{{cite book | first=L. | last=van den Dries | title=Tame topology and o-minimal structures | series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series | volume=248 | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | year=1998 | zbl=0953.03045 | page=31 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Khovanskii | first=A. G. | authorlink= Askold Khovanskii | title=Fewnomials | others= Translated from the Russian by Smilka Zdravkovska | zbl=0728.12002 | series=Translations of Mathematical Monographs | volume=88 | location=Providence, RI | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | year=1991 | isbn=0-8218-4547-0 }}</ref> Related fields are [[O-minimal|o-minimal theory]] and [[Subanalytic set|real analytic geometry]].

Examples: [[Real plane curve]]s are examples of real algebraic sets and [[Polyhedron|polyhedra]] are examples of semialgebraic sets. Real [[algebraic function]]s and [[Nash function]]s are examples of semialgebraic mappings. Piecewise polynomial mappings (see the [[Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture]]) are also semialgebraic mappings.

'''Computational real algebraic geometry''' is concerned with the algorithmic aspects of real algebraic (and semialgebraic) geometry. The main algorithm is [[cylindrical algebraic decomposition]]. It is used to cut semialgebraic sets into nice pieces and to compute their projections.

'''Real algebra''' is the part of algebra which is relevant to real algebraic (and semialgebraic) geometry. It is mostly concerned with the study of [[ordered field]]s and [[ordered ring]]s (in particular [[real closed field]]s) and their applications to the study of [[positive polynomial]]s and [[Polynomial SOS|sums-of-squares of polynomials]]. (See [[Hilbert's seventeenth problem|Hilbert's 17th problem]] and the [[Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz]].) The relation of real algebra to real algebraic geometry is similar to the relation of [[commutative algebra]] to [[complex algebraic geometry]]. Related fields are the theory of [[moment problem]]s, [[convex optimization]], the theory of [[quadratic forms]], [[valuation theory]] and [[model theory]].

==Timeline of real algebra and real algebraic geometry==

* 1826 [[Fourier–Motzkin elimination|Fourier's algorithm]] for systems of linear inequalities.<ref>[[Joseph Fourier|Joseph B. J. Fourier]], Solution d'une question particuliére du calcul des inégalités. Bull. sci. Soc. Philomn. Paris 99–100. OEuvres 2, 315–319.</ref> Rediscovered by [[Lloyd Dines]] in 1919<ref>{{cite journal|authorlink=Lloyd Dines|first=Lloyd L. |last=Dines|title= Systems of linear inequalities|journal= [[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=(2) |volume= 20  |year=1919|issue=3|pages=191–199|doi=10.2307/1967869 |jstor=1967869 }}</ref> and [[Theodore Motzkin]] in 1936.<ref>[[Theodore Motzkin]], Beiträge zur Theorie der linearen Ungleichungen. IV+ 76 S. Diss., Basel (1936).</ref>
* 1835 [[Sturm's theorem]] on real root counting<ref>[[Jacques Charles François Sturm]], Mémoires divers présentés par des savants étrangers 6, pp. 273–318 (1835).</ref>
* 1856 Hermite's theorem on real root counting.<ref>[[Charles Hermite]], Sur le Nombre des Racines d’une Équation Algébrique Comprise Entre des Limites Données, [[Crelle's Journal|Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]], vol. 52, pp. 39–51 (1856).</ref>
* 1876 [[Harnack's curve theorem]].<ref>[[Carl Gustav Axel Harnack|C. G. A. Harnack]] Über Vieltheiligkeit der ebenen algebraischen Curven, [[Mathematische Annalen]] 10 (1876), 189–199</ref> (This bound on the number of components was later extended to all [[Betti number]]s of all real algebraic sets<ref>I. G. Petrovski˘ı and O. A. Ole˘ınik, On the topology of real algebraic surfaces, Izvestiya Akad. Nauk SSSR. Ser.Mat. 13, (1949). 389–402</ref><ref>[[John Milnor]], On the Betti numbers of real varieties, [[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]] '''15''' (1964), 275–280.</ref><ref>[[René Thom]], Sur l’homologie des vari´et´es algebriques r´eelles, in: S. S. Cairns (ed.), Differential and Combinatorial Topology, pp. 255–265, [[Princeton University Press]], Princeton, NJ, 1965.</ref> and all semialgebraic sets.<ref>{{cite journal|first=Saugata|last= Basu|title= On bounding the Betti numbers and computing the Euler characteristic of semi-algebraic sets|journal= [[Discrete & Computational Geometry]] |volume=22 |year=1999|issue= 1|pages= 1–18|doi= 10.1007/PL00009443|s2cid= 7023328|hdl= 2027.42/42421|hdl-access= free}}</ref>)
* 1888 Hilbert's theorem on ternary quartics.<ref>{{cite journal|first=David|last=Hilbert|authorlink=David Hilbert|title=Uber die Darstellung definiter Formen als Summe von Formenquadraten|journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]]|volume= 32|pages= 342–350 |year=1888|issue=3 |doi=10.1007/BF01443605 |s2cid=177804714 |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1428214 }}</ref>
* 1900 [[Hilbert's problems]] (especially the [[Hilbert's sixteenth problem|16th]] and the [[Hilbert's seventeenth problem|17th]] problem)
* 1902 [[Farkas' lemma]]<ref>{{cite journal|authorlink=Gyula Farkas (natural scientist)|first=Julius|last=Farkas|url=http://dz-srv1.sub.uni-goettingen.de/sub/digbib/loader?ht=VIEW&did=D261364|title=Über die Theorie der Einfachen Ungleichungen|journal=[[Crelle's Journal|Journal für die Reine und Angewandte Mathematik]]|volume=124|pages=1–27|archive-date=2007-03-10|access-date=2010-07-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070310185722/http://dz-srv1.sub.uni-goettingen.de/sub/digbib/loader?ht=VIEW&did=D261364|url-status=dead}}</ref> (Can be reformulated as linear positivstellensatz.)
*1914 [[Annibale Comessatti]] showed that not every real algebraic surface is birational to '''RP'''<sup>''2''</sup><ref>{{cite journal|first=Annibale |last=Comessatti|title= Sulla connessione delle superfizie razionali reali| journal=Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata |volume=23|issue=3|year=1914|pages= 215–283|doi=10.1007/BF02419577 |s2cid=121297483 |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1947509 }}</ref>
* 1916 Fejér's conjecture about nonnegative trigonometric polynomials.<ref>[[Lipót Fejér]], ¨Uber trigonometrische Polynome, J. Reine Angew. Math. 146 (1916), 53–82.</ref> (Solved by [[Frigyes Riesz]].<ref>[[Frigyes Riesz]] and [[Béla Szőkefalvi-Nagy]], Functional Analysis, Frederick Ungar Publ. Co., New York, 1955.</ref>)
* 1927 [[Emil Artin]]'s solution of [[Hilbert's 17th problem]]<ref>{{cite journal|first=Emil|last= Artin|authorlink=Emil Artin|title= Uber die Zerlegung definiter Funktionen in Quadrate|journal= Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg|volume= 5 |year=1927|pages= 85–99|doi= 10.1007/BF02952512|s2cid= 122881707}}</ref>
* 1927 Krull–Baer Theorem<ref>{{cite journal| first=Wolfgang|last=Krull| authorlink=Wolfgang Krull|title= Allgemeine Bewertungstheorie|journal= [[Crelle's Journal|Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]|volume= 1932|pages= 160–196 |year=1932|issue=167 |doi=10.1515/crll.1932.167.160 |s2cid=199547002 }}</ref><ref>{{citation|first=Reinhold| last=Baer| authorlink=Reinhold Baer| title= Über nicht-archimedisch geordnete Körper |journal= Sitzungsberichte der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften. Mathematisch-Naturwissenschaftliche Klasse|volume= 8|pages= 3–13 |year=1927}}</ref> (connection between orderings and valuations)
* 1928 Pólya's Theorem on positive polynomials on a simplex<ref>[[George Pólya]], Über positive Darstellung von Polynomen Vierteljschr, Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 73 (1928) 141–145, in: [[R. P. Boas|R.P. Boas]] (Ed.), Collected Papers Vol. 2, MIT Press, Cambridge, MA, 1974, pp. 309–313</ref>
* 1929 [[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden|B. L. van der Waerden]] sketches a proof that real algebraic and [[semialgebraic set]]s are triangularizable,<ref>[[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden|B. L. van der Waerden]], Topologische Begründung des Kalküls der abzählenden Geometrie. Math. Ann. 102, 337–362 (1929).</ref> but the necessary tools have not been developed to make the argument rigorous.
* 1931 [[Alfred Tarski]]'s [[Tarski–Seidenberg theorem|real quantifier elimination]].<ref>[[Alfred Tarski]], A decision method for elementary algebra and geometry, Rand. Corp.. 1948; UC Press, Berkeley, 1951, Announced in : Ann. Soc. Pol. Math. 9 (1930, published 1931) 206–7; and in Fund. Math. 17 (1931) 210–239.</ref> Improved and popularized by [[Abraham Seidenberg]] in 1954.<ref>[[Abraham Seidenberg]], A new decision method for elementary algebra, [[Annals of Mathematics]] 60 (1954), 365–374.</ref> (Both use [[Sturm's theorem]].)
* 1936 [[Herbert Seifert]] proved that every closed smooth submanifold of <math>\R^n</math> with trivial normal bundle, can be isotoped to a component of a nonsingular real algebraic subset of <math>\R^n</math> which is a complete intersection<ref>[[Herbert Seifert]], Algebraische approximation von Mannigfaltigkeiten, [[Mathematische Zeitschrift]] 41 (1936), 1–17</ref> (from the conclusion of this theorem the word "component" can not be removed<ref>[[Selman Akbulut]] and Henry C. King, Submanifolds and homology of nonsingular real algebraic varieties, [[American Journal of Mathematics]],  vol. 107, no. 1   (Feb., 1985)  p.72</ref>).
* 1940 [[Marshall Stone]]'s representation theorem for partially ordered rings.<ref>{{cite journal|first=Marshall|last=Stone|authorlink=Marshall Stone|title=  A general theory of spectra. I. |journal= [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]] |volume= 26|year=1940|issue=4 |pages= 280–283|doi=10.1073/pnas.26.4.280 |pmid=16588355 |pmc=1078172 |doi-access=free |bibcode=1940PNAS...26..280S }}</ref> Improved by [[Richard Kadison]] in 1951<ref>{{citation|authorlink=Richard Kadison|first=Richard V. |last=Kadison|title= A representation theory for commutative topological algebra|journal= [[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=7| pages=39 pp |year=1951|mr=0044040}}</ref> and Donald Dubois in 1967<ref>{{cite journal|last=Dubois|first= Donald W. |title=A note on David Harrison's theory of preprimes|journal= [[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]]  |volume=21 |year=1967|pages= 15–19|doi= 10.2140/pjm.1967.21.15 |mr=0209200|s2cid= 120262803 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.pjm/1102992597|doi-access=free}}</ref> (Kadison–Dubois representation theorem). Further improved by Mihai Putinar in 1993<ref>Mihai Putinar, Positive polynomials on compact semi-algebraic sets. [[Indiana University Mathematics Journal]] 42  (1993),  no. 3, 969–984.</ref> and Jacobi in 2001<ref>T. Jacobi, A representation theorem for certain partially ordered commutative rings. [[Mathematische Zeitschrift]]  237  (2001),  no. 2, 259–273.</ref> (Putinar–Jacobi representation theorem).
*1952 [[John Forbes Nash Jr.|John Nash]] proved that every closed smooth manifold is diffeomorphic to a nonsingular component of a real algebraic set.<ref>{{cite journal|authorlink=John Forbes Nash Jr.|first=John|last= Nash | title= Real algebraic manifolds|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=56 |year=1952|issue=3 |pages= 405–421|doi=10.2307/1969649 |jstor=1969649 }}</ref>
* 1956 [[Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture]] formulated.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Garrett|last1= Birkhoff|author1-link= Garrett Birkhoff |first2=Richard Scott|last2= Pierce|title= Lattice ordered rings|journal= Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências|volume= 28 |year=1956|pages= 41–69}}</ref> (Solved in dimensions ≤ 2.<ref>{{cite journal|first=Louis|last= Mahé|title= On the Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture| journal=[[Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics]]|volume= 14 |year=1984| issue= 4|pages= 983–985|mr=0773148|doi=10.1216/RMJ-1984-14-4-983|doi-access=free}}</ref>)
* 1964 [[Stengle's Positivstellensatz|Krivine's Nullstellensatz and Positivestellensatz]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Krivine | first1=J.-L. | url=http://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/docs/00/16/56/58/PDF/Anneaux_preordonnes.pdf | title=Anneaux préordonnés | journal= [[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]] | volume=12 | date=1964 | pages=307–326 | doi=10.1007/BF02807438 | doi-access=free}}</ref> Rediscovered and popularized by Stengle in 1974.<ref>G. Stengle,  A nullstellensatz and a positivstellensatz in semialgebraic geometry.  Math. Ann.  207  (1974), 87–97.</ref> (Krivine uses [[Tarski–Seidenberg theorem|real quantifier elimination]] while Stengle uses Lang's homomorphism theorem.<ref>S. Lang, Algebra. Addison–Wesley Publishing Co., Inc., Reading, Mass. 1965 xvii+508 pp.</ref>)
*1964 Lojasiewicz triangulated semi-analytic sets<ref>S.  Lojasiewicz, Triangulation of semi-analytic sets, Ann. Scu. Norm. di Pisa, 18 (1964), 449–474.</ref>
*1964 [[Heisuke Hironaka]] proved the resolution of singularity theorem<ref>[[Heisuke Hironaka]], Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero. I, [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2) 79 (1): (1964) 109–203, and part II, pp. 205–326.</ref>
*1964 [[Hassler Whitney]] proved that every analytic variety admits a stratification satisfying the [[Whitney conditions]].<ref>[[Hassler Whitney]], Local properties of analytic varieties, Differential and combinatorial topology (ed. S. Cairns), Princeton Univ. Press, Princeton N.J. (1965), 205–244.</ref>
* 1967 [[Theodore Motzkin]] finds a positive polynomial which is not a [[Polynomial SOS|sum of squares of polynomials]].<ref>[[Theodore Motzkin|Theodore S. Motzkin]],  The arithmetic-geometric inequality.  1967 Inequalities (Proc. Sympos. Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, 1965)  pp. 205–224 {{MR|0223521}}.</ref>
* 1972 [[Vladimir Abramovich Rokhlin|Vladimir Rokhlin]] proved [[Gudkov's conjecture]].<ref>"[https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/rohlin3.pdf Proof of Gudkov's hypothesis]". V. A. Rokhlin. ''Functional Analysis and Its Applications'', volume 6, pp. 136–138 (1972)</ref>
* 1973 [[Alberto Tognoli]] proved that every closed smooth manifold is diffeomorphic to a nonsingular real algebraic set.<ref>[[Alberto Tognoli]], Su una congettura di Nash, Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa 27, 167–185 (1973).</ref>
* 1975 [[George E. Collins]] discovers [[cylindrical algebraic decomposition]] algorithm, which improves Tarski's real [[quantifier elimination]] and allows to implement it on a computer.<ref>[[George E. Collins]],  "Quantifier elimination for real closed fields by cylindrical algebraic decomposition", Lect. Notes Comput. Sci. 33, 134–183, 1975 {{MR|0403962}}.</ref>
* 1973 [[Jean-Louis Verdier]] proved that every subanalytic set admits a stratification with condition (w).<ref>[[Jean-Louis Verdier]], Stratifications de Whitney et théorème de Bertini-Sard, [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 36, 295–312 (1976).</ref>
* 1979 Michel Coste and [[Marie-Françoise Roy]] discover the real spectrum of a commutative ring.<ref>[[Marie-Françoise Roy|Marie-Françoise Coste-Roy]], Michel Coste, Topologies for real algebraic geometry.  Topos theoretic methods in geometry,  pp. 37–100, Various Publ. Ser., 30, Aarhus Univ., Aarhus, 1979.</ref>
*1980 [[Oleg Viro]] introduced the "patch working" technique and used it to classify real algebraic curves of low degree.<ref>[[Oleg Viro|Oleg Ya. Viro]], Gluing of plane real algebraic curves and constructions of curves of degrees 6 and 7. In Topology (Leningrad, 1982), volume 1060 of [[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]], pages 187–200. Springer, Berlin, 1984</ref> Later Ilya Itenberg and Viro used it to produce counterexamples to the [[Ragsdale conjecture]],<ref>{{cite journal| last=Viro | first=Oleg Ya. | authorlink=Oleg Viro | year=1980 | title=Кривые степени 7, кривые степени 8 и гипотеза Рэгсдейл |trans-title=Curves of degree 7, curves of degree 8 and the hypothesis of Ragsdale | journal=[[Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR]] | volume=254 | issue=6 | pages=1306–1309}} Translated in {{cite journal| title=Curves of degree 7, curves of degree 8 and Ragsdale's conjecture | journal=Soviet Mathematics - Doklady | volume=22 | pages=566–570 | year=1980 | zbl=0422.14032 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Itenberg | first1=Ilia | last2=Mikhalkin | first2=Grigory | last3=Shustin | first3=Eugenii | title=Tropical algebraic geometry | zbl=1162.14300 | series=Oberwolfach Seminars | volume=35 | location=Basel | publisher=Birkhäuser | isbn=978-3-7643-8309-1 | year=2007 | pages=34–35 }}</ref> and [[Grigory Mikhalkin]] applied it to [[tropical geometry]] for curve counting.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Grigory|last= Mikhalkin|title= Enumerative tropical algebraic geometry in <math>\R^2</math>|journal= [[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=18 |year=2005|pages= 313–377|doi= 10.1090/S0894-0347-05-00477-7|doi-access= free}}</ref>
*1980 [[Selman Akbulut]] and Henry C. King gave a topological characterization of real algebraic sets with isolated singularities, and topologically characterized nonsingular real algebraic sets (not necessarily compact)<ref>[[Selman Akbulut]] and Henry C. King, The topology of real algebraic sets with isolated singularities, [[Annals of Mathematics]] 113 (1981), 425–446.</ref>
*1980 Akbulut and King proved that every knot in <math>S^n</math> is the link of a real algebraic set with isolated singularity in  <math>\R^{n+1}</math><ref>[[Selman Akbulut]] and Henry C. King, All knots are algebraic, [[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]] 56, Fasc. 3 (1981), 339–351.</ref>
*1981 Akbulut and King proved that every compact PL manifold is PL homeomorphic to a real algebraic set.<ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King, Real algebraic structures on topological spaces,
[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]] 53 (1981), 79–162.</ref><ref>S. Akbulut and L. Taylor, A topological resolution theorem, 
[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]] 53 (1981), 163–196.</ref><ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King, The topology of real algebraic sets, 
L'Enseignement Mathématique 29 (1983), 221–261.</ref>
*1983 Akbulut and King introduced "Topological Resolution Towers" as topological models of real algebraic sets, from this they obtained new topological invariants of real algebraic sets, and topologically characterized all 3-dimensional algebraic sets.<ref>Selman Akbulut and Henry C. King, Topology of real algebraic sets, MSRI Pub, 25. Springer-Verlag, New York (1992) {{ISBN|0-387-97744-9}}</ref>  These invariants later generalized by Michel Coste and Krzysztof Kurdyka<ref>
{{cite journal | last1=Coste | first1=Michel | last2=Kurdyka | first2=Krzysztof | title=On the link of a stratum in a real algebraic set | journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]] |  volume=31 | issue=2 | year=1992 |  doi=10.1016/0040-9383(92)90025-d | pages=323–336 | mr=1167174 | doi-access=free }}</ref> as well as Clint McCrory and Adam Parusiński.<ref>{{citation|first1=Clint|last1= McCrory|first2= Adam|last2= Parusiński|contribution= Algebraically constructible functions: real algebra and topology| arxiv=math/0202086|title=Arc spaces and additive invariants in real algebraic and analytic geometry|pages= 69–85|
series=Panoramas et Synthèses|volume= 24|publisher= [[Société mathématique de France]] |location= Paris|year= 2007|mr=2409689}}</ref>
* 1984 Ludwig Bröcker's theorem on minimal generation of basic open [[semialgebraic set]]s<ref>{{cite journal | last=Bröcker | first=Ludwig | title=Minimale erzeugung von Positivbereichen | journal=[[Geometriae Dedicata]] | volume=16 | issue=3 | year=1984 | pages=335–350| doi=10.1007/bf00147875 | language=de | mr=0765338| s2cid=117475206 }}
</ref> (improved and extended to basic closed [[semialgebraic set]]s by Scheiderer.<ref>C. Scheiderer,  Stability index of real varieties.  [[Inventiones Mathematicae]]  97  (1989),  no. 3, 467–483.</ref>)
*1984 Benedetti and Dedo proved that not every closed smooth manifold is diffeomorphic to a totally algebraic nonsingular real algebraic set (totally algebraic means all its Z/2Z-homology cycles are represented by real algebraic subsets).<ref>R. Benedetti and M. Dedo,  Counterexamples to representing homology classes by real algebraic subvarieties up to homeomorphism, [[Compositio Mathematica]], 53, (1984), 143–151.</ref>
*1991 Akbulut and King proved that every closed smooth manifold is homeomorphic to a totally algebraic real algebraic set.<ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King, All compact manifolds are homeomorphic to totally algebraic real algebraic sets, [[Comment. Math. Helv.]] 66 (1991) 139–149.</ref>
* 1991 Schmüdgen's solution of the multidimensional moment problem for compact semialgebraic sets and related strict positivstellensatz.<ref>K. Schmüdgen,  The ''K''-moment problem for compact semi-algebraic sets.  Math. Ann.  289  (1991),  no. 2, 203–206.</ref> Algebraic proof found by Wörmann.<ref>T. Wörmann Strikt Positive Polynome in der Semialgebraischen Geometrie, Univ. Dortmund 1998.</ref> Implies Reznick's version of Artin's theorem with uniform denominators.<ref>B. Reznick, Uniform denominators in Hilbert's seventeenth problem.  Math. Z.  220  (1995),  no. 1, 75–97.</ref>
*1992 Akbulut and King proved ambient versions of the Nash-Tognoli theorem: Every closed smooth submanifold of '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> is isotopic to the nonsingular points (component) of a real algebraic subset of '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>, and they extended this result to immersed submanifolds of '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>.<ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King On approximating submanifolds by algebraic sets and a solution to the Nash conjecture, [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 107 (1992), 87–98</ref><ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King,  Algebraicity of Immersions, [[Topology (journal)|Topology]], vol. 31, no. 4, (1992), 701–712.</ref>
*1992 Benedetti and Marin proved that every compact closed smooth 3-manifold '''M''' can be obtained from <math>S^3</math> by a sequence of blow ups and downs along smooth centers, and that '''M''' is homeomorphic to a possibly singular affine real algebraic rational threefold<ref>R. Benedetti and A. Marin, Déchirures de variétés de dimension trois ...., [[Comment. Math. Helv.]] 67 (1992), 514–545.</ref>
*1997 Bierstone and Milman proved a canonical resolution of singularities theorem<ref>E. Bierstone and P.D. Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero by blowing up the maximum strata of a local invariant, [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 128 (2) (1997) 207–302.</ref>
*1997 Mikhalkin proved that every closed smooth n-manifold can be obtained from <math>S^n</math> by a sequence of topological blow ups and downs<ref>G. Mikhalkin, Blow up equivalence of smooth closed manifolds, [[Topology (journal)|Topology]], 36 (1997) 287–299</ref>
*1998 [[János Kollár]] showed that not every closed 3-manifold is a projective real 3-fold which is birational to  '''RP'''<sup>''3''</sup><ref>[[János Kollár]], The Nash conjecture for algebraic threefolds, ERA of AMS 4 (1998) 63–73</ref>
* 2000 Scheiderer's local-global principle and related non-strict extension of Schmüdgen's positivstellensatz in dimensions ≤ 2.<ref>C. Scheiderer,  Sums of squares of regular functions on real algebraic varieties. [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]  352  (2000),  no. 3, 1039–1069.</ref><ref>C. Scheiderer,  Sums of squares on real algebraic curves, [[Mathematische Zeitschrift]]  245  (2003),  no. 4, 725–760.</ref><ref>C. Scheiderer,  Sums of squares on real algebraic surfaces.  Manuscripta Mathematica 119  (2006),  no. 4, 395–410.</ref>
*2000 [[János Kollár]] proved that every closed smooth 3–manifold is the real part of a compact complex manifold which can be obtained from  <math>\mathbb{CP}^3</math> by a sequence of real blow ups and blow downs.<ref>[[János Kollár]], The Nash conjecture for nonprojective threefolds, arXiv:math/0009108v1</ref>
*2003 Welschinger introduces an invariant for counting real rational curves<ref>J.-Y. Welschinger, Invariants of real rational symplectic 4-manifolds and lower bounds in real enumerative geometry, [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 162 (2005), no. 1, 195–234.  {{zbl|1082.14052}}</ref>
*2005 Akbulut and King showed that not every nonsingular real algebraic subset of '''RP'''<sup>''n''</sup> is smoothly isotopic to the real part of a nonsingular complex algebraic subset of '''CP'''<sup>''n''</sup><ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King, Transcendental submanifolds of '''RP'''<sup>''n''</sup> [[Comment. Math. Helv.]], 80, (2005), 427–432</ref><ref>S. Akbulut, Real algebraic structures, Proceedings of GGT, (2005) 49–58, arXiv:math/0601105v3.</ref>
